abstract: The sixth reported case of choriocarcinoma associated with transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of the bladder is described. A 67-year-old female presented with haematuria and was found to have a bladder tumour with both poorly differentiated TCC and trophoblastic elements. The tumour was confirmed as being limited to the bladder at laparotomy. The patient was treated with combination chemotherapy but, after an initial response, relapsed and died of disease. Postmortem examination revealed multiple metastatic choriocarcinoma and no TCC. A review of the clinical evolution in the reported cases suggests that transitional cell carcinoma is the cell of origin of these tumours by the process of progressive retrodifferentiation.
abstract_ja: 絨毛癌と膀胱移行上皮癌の併存例で、6例目の報告である。67歳女性が血尿を主訴に受診し、膀胱腫瘍を認めた。腫瘍は低分化型移行上皮癌と栄養膜成分の両方を含んでいた。開腹術で腫瘍が膀胱に限局していることが確認された。併用化学療法を施行したが、初期には奏効したものの再発し、死亡した。剖検では多発性の転移性絨毛癌がみられ、移行上皮癌は認められなかった。既報告例の臨床経過を検討すると、移行上皮癌が進行性の逆分化(retrodifferentiation)を経てこれらの腫瘍を生じる起源細胞であることが示唆される。
